title: Find Largest Number
summary: Return the largest value in an integer array, and define what happens when the array is empty.
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest value it contains.

Interviewers love this warm-up because the interesting part is the **contract**, not the loop:
if `nums` is empty there is no largest value, so your method must throw an
`IllegalArgumentException` instead of returning a made-up number like `0` or `Integer.MIN_VALUE`.
constraints: If nums is empty, throw IllegalArgumentException

examples.explanation: All values are negative; the answer is still one of them.
An empty array has no largest value.

hints: What value should `largest` start at so that it's guaranteed to be a real element of the array?
Seed your answer with the first element, then scan the rest, replacing it whenever you see something bigger. Check the empty case before you touch nums[0].

if nums is empty: throw IllegalArgumentException
largest = nums[0]
for each n in nums:
    if n > largest: largest = n
return largest

Starting from 0 is the classic bug: it returns 0 for an all-negative array. Starting from nums[0] guarantees the answer is a real element. A single pass visits every element once, so it runs in O(n) time with O(1) extra space. The empty-array guard makes the contract explicit instead of crashing with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
